hypothesis: The destabilisation in run 1 was caused by the angular_momentum_reward_weight jump (-0.01→-0.05), which competed with the torso dynamics needed for balance. Reverting it to -0.01 while keeping gait_phase_regularity_reward_weight at -2.5 and pose_std_walking_shoulder_pitch at 0.35 isolates whether the stronger regularity penalty alone can reduce gait CV metrics toward the healthy range (<0.15) without instability. The shoulder pitch loosening gives arms the kinematic freedom to swing; the regularity penalty shapes the timing without the destabilising angular momentum conflict.
expected_effects: fell_over_rate drops back toward 0 by iteration ~500 — reverting angular_momentum_reward_weight removes the destabilising force (stability gate should pass this time)
gait_contact_cv_mean decreases from 0.567 baseline toward <0.3 — primary effect of the stronger regularity penalty without the competing angular momentum term
gait_air_cv_mean decreases from 0.270 — secondary CV improvement from more periodic swing cadence
track_linear_velocity reward decreases slightly — expected Rule 6 trade-off confirming the regularity weight is doing real work (if it doesn't dip, the weight change isn't taking effect)
symmetry_vel_cost_mean improves modestly — more regular gait timing should reduce velocity asymmetry between legs
